about: Agent Behaviour Policy (ABP) for PrompTugal__IaC. CI reads this file on every run: a pipeline may take only the actions listed for it, an agent's commits may change only the paths listed for it, and every privilege held by the GitHub App or an AWS role is listed here with its reason. Anything not listed is refused. Changes to this file, to .github/ and to build/ are Dinis's: they reach dev only as pull requests he merges.
source: Dinis, 25 Nov 2026 (relayed by cl-6.maestro@dinis): "we also need the super important (and powerful) PrompTugal__IaC since (managed by the PrompTugal__Agent__Infrastructure agent) since that is the one that will manage all PrompTugal GitHub and AWS resources/changes". Dinis, 25 Nov 2026 ~22:51 UTC in cl-6.infra's session: "yes let's set this up on PrompTugal so that you have access to both AWS and GiHub". Pattern: SovereignWebsite/SovereignWebsite__IaC.

never: print, commit or read a private key or token
hold a credential (the GitHub App and the AWS role are CI's)
name a private person without consent
delete, transfer, archive or make private a repository
cl-6.infra@PrompTugal.dinis.source: Started by cl-6.maestro@dinis at Dinis's word, 25 Nov 2026 22:48 UTC.

checks.note: Tests, policy validation, leak scan, signed commits and policy paths, and a dry plan of the organisation checked against this policy. No secrets.

runs_on: push to dev that changes org/ or policy/
org-apply.note: Creates and configures only. A repository that exists but is not in org/repos.json is reported, never deleted. On an existing repository it changes only the default branch (to dev) and the settings its own entry in org/repos.json names; the defaults block applies only when a repository is created. It never changes visibility.
org-apply.default_branch_rule: Every repository has dev as its default branch; Org apply creates dev from the current default branch if it is missing, then sets it. Dinis, 25 Nov 2026, relayed by cl-6.maestro@dinis: "please make note to the Infa agent that all repos should have a default dev branch"; confirmed in cl-6.infra's session ~22:51 UTC: "yes".
org-apply.pages_note: pages.enable turns on GitHub Pages from dev (root) for a repository whose entry sets pages_site; pages.set_cname sets only the site its entry names, under *.agent.promptugal.news. Its DNS record is added to org/dns.json only after the custom domain is set, so no record ever points at a site that is not ours.
org-apply.pages_source: Dinis, 26 Nov 2026 in cl-6.infra's session: "go ahead with the sites"; "you should already have permission".
org-apply.team_note: team.grant_push gives a team that a repository's own entry names push (write) on that repository; team.grant_admin and team.grant_maintain stay refused always. Dinis, 26 Nov 2026 in cl-6.infra's session: "You need to add this team to all the repos you created, or else nobody else can edit it" (team promptugal-news-agents).
org-apply.https_note: pages.enforce_https turns on HTTPS for an agent site (its own *.agent.promptugal.news domain) only once GitHub reports its certificate approved or issued; until then the run notes it and the next run tries again. Dinis, 26 Nov 2026 in cl-6.infra's session: "go ahead with the HTTPS for the sites".
org-apply.nudge_note: pages.nudge_certificate clears an agent site's custom domain and sets the same one again, so GitHub re-checks DNS and requests the certificate; only when there is none or it failed, never while one is pending. The domains were set before their DNS records existed (run 45742880611: 77 sites with no certificate requested). The same fix SovereignWebsite__IaC uses.

check-github-app.note: Mints the App's token and lists the repositories it can see. Changes nothing.

runs_on: push to dev that changes org/dns.json
dns-apply.note: CREATE only: a record listed in org/dns.json that the zone lacks. One that exists with another value is reported, never changed. Names only under *.promptugal.news (the apex, with its Google verification and SPF TXT records, is never written). The AWS role enforces the same limits (docs/aws-oidc.md).
dns-apply.source: Dinis, 25 Nov 2026 in cl-6.infra's session: "are you able to create um, repos here and also map the DNS?"; zone ID ~23:50 UTC.
dns-apply.claims_note: DNS apply also mints a read-only App token (metadata read, pages read) to list the custom domains PrompTugal repositories claim. It never creates a CNAME to *.github.io that no repository claims, and it reports every record in the zone pointing at GitHub Pages that no repository claims (a takeover risk). Found by cl-6.security@PrompTugal.dinis on fringe.promptugal.news, 26 Nov 2026, relayed by cl-6.maestro@dinis.
